extraction.name: ACL OCL Corpus
extraction.description: A scholarly corpus derived from the ACL Anthology to assist Open scientific research in the Computational Linguistics domain. The corpus spans seven decades, containing 73K papers, alongside 210K figures, with metadata, PDF files, citation graphs and structured full texts with sections, figures, and links to Semantic Scholar.
extraction.creator: Shaurya Rohatgi, Yanxia Qin, Benjamin Aw, Niranjana Unnithan, Min-Yen Kan
extraction.publisher: National University of Singapore, Pennsylvania State University
extraction.rai:dataCollection: We start by crawling the PDF files and metadata from the source ACL Anthology. We design crawlers to fetch all the PDF documents and metadata from its website. We remove PDF files longer than 50 pages, which are mostly conference volume introductions or handbooks. We then obtain 73,285 conference journal and workshop papers in the CL domain. The dataset undergoes annual updates, during which we download and process papers recently added to the ACL Anthology. For these updates, we identify new additions by monitoring changes in URLs.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: PDF files and metadata from the ACL Anthology website. The ACL Anthology digitally archives all scientific papers in the CL domain, including metadata, PDF files, and supplementary materials.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: We pass the PDF files through the full-text extraction process using GROBID for the full-text extraction from PDF files. We take the S2ORC-JSON format for our full-text schema, which includes complete information parsed from PDF files, such as metadata, authors, and body text with citations, references, sections and etc. We extract figures and tables from PDF files using PDFFigures. Each extracted figure is associated with its caption texts, which show the figure ID and textual description in the paper. The figures are stored separately from the textual data in OCL. We remove PDF files longer than 50 pages.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For topic classification, we crawl published papers of several online held CL conferences (e.g., ACL 2020, EACL 2021) between 2020 and 2022, together with their topics from those websites. After aligning those papers with the data in the ACL OCL, we obtained 2545 documents classified in 21 topics in total. We train a pre-trained language model (PLM) based topic classification method on a subset of 2,545 scientific papers with ground truth topic labels. We then extrapolate and integrate the model predictions as silver-labeled topic information in the OCL.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Model-predicted silver topic labels are released together with OCL. The best performance achieved by the PLM-based supervised method is comparable to those reported in the state-of-the-art topic classification tasks on the scientific domain. From the last column in Table 3 (system-predicted topics), we observe 13 correct labels out of 15 documents. Two works in Resource & Evaluation, namely BLEU and ROUGE, are incorrectly predicted due to insufficient training samples and high overlap with other topics. The 87% accuracy is higher than an expected 69% accuracy tested on the STop test set.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GROBID for full-text extraction from PDF files, PDFFigures for figure and table extraction, language detection toolkit for language detection, BART-large-MNLI for zero-shot topic classification, SciBERT and SPECTER for PLM-based topic classification
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset undergoes annual updates, during which we download and process papers recently added to the ACL Anthology. For these updates, we identify new additions by monitoring changes in URLs. In the future, we will work on the data currency of OCL, which aims to keep OCL up-to-date with the ACL Anthology data. We plan to update OCL by year to keep it alive.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The OCL corpus is a small-scale collection of documents specifically focusing on peer-reviewed and open-access CL papers. As a result, it is not a comprehensive corpus like S2ORC, since it does not include any other sources beyond the ACL Anthology. Due to the limitations of GROBID in formatting information extraction such as figures, some common issues include missing section names, merged paragraphs, the mixing of footnotes with texts, and misidentifying texts as table captions. GROBID also struggles with the extraction of tables and figures, especially in-line equations. Incorrect metadata such as author names exceeding three tokens, is a common issue. There are 19 sections not detected from 21 scientific papers. All footnote numbers are concatenated to the body text. There are 28.78% (19/66) figures not detected. There are 76 tables in total, 31.58% (24) of them are not detected and 46.06% (35) are detected but with either wrong contents or titles.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The OCL corpus is an open research-oriented scholarly dataset that aims to provide comprehensive and fundamental information about scientific papers. Use cases include: temporal topic trends analysis, emerging topic detection, evolution detection of topics, paper-reviewer matching, document-level terminology detection, coreference resolution, pre-training scientific large language models, fine-tuning general LLMs, building scientific assistants for the CL domain, summarization and related work generation tasks, contribution extraction from Introductions and Conclusions, future work prediction from Conclusions, analysis of generalization ability of NLP models from Experiments, examining modifications made to pre-print versions, analyzing historical language change in the CL domain, construction of knowledge graphs, multimodal research tasks such as summarization which integrates text summaries with figures and citation visualizations.
